card.why: Replaces the second rice crop with maize and adds groundnut, lowering paddy water use and diversifying crop families.
evidence: Climate analogs (enso = el_nino, n=9): 1991, 1997, 2002, 2004, 2006, 2009, 2015, 2018, 2023. Seasonal rainfall and ET0 from NASA POWER daily data (1991-2025).
Irrigation need 158 mm per rotation year on average; 440 mm in the worst 20 % of analog years.
49% of the site area has slopes above 10 % (SRTM).
benefits: Living cover 96% of the year vs 67% now.
More legume months, which add biological nitrogen.
Less rain falling on bare soil, lowering erosion exposure.
More changes of crop family, which can interrupt pest cycles.
gaps: Soil drainage class is not available for Banyumas at field scale.
Rainfall and soil wetness come from NASA POWER (reanalysis-based, ~0.5 degree).
SMAP satellite soil moisture not yet included.
MODIS NDVI (bare-field timing, crop stress) not yet included.
ET0 uses Hargreaves-Samani from temperature; months outside the modelled seasons are not counted.
Crop prices, yields and labour are not modelled.
risks_for_local_review: Maize and groundnut need well-drained fields; check drainage locally.
Market access for maize and groundnut must be confirmed.
